arxiv-2109-05212.title: Memory from coupled instabilities in unfolded crumpled sheets
arxiv-2109-05212.creator: Dor Shohat, Daniel Hexner, Yoav Lahini
arxiv-2109-05212.description: Abstract Crumpling an ordinary thin sheet transforms it into a structure with unusual mechanical behaviors, such as enhanced rigidity, emission of crackling noise, slow relaxations, and memory retention. A central challenge in explaining these behaviours lies in understanding the contribution of the complex geometry of the sheet.

arxiv-2206-14900.title: Phases of 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models
arxiv-2206-14900.description: Abstract We study 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 supersymmetric Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) models with complex fermions at non-zero background charge. Motivated by multi-charge supersymmetric black holes, we propose a new 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 SYK model with multiple U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) symmetries, integer charges, and a non-vanishing supersymmetric index, realizing features not present in known SYK models.

arxiv-2303-16814.title: Hyperbolic width functions and characterizations of bodies of constant width in the hyperbolic space
arxiv-2303-16814.creator: Károly J. Böröczky, András Csépai, Ádám Sagmeister
arxiv-2303-16814.description: Abstract . We discuss basic properties of several different width functions in the n n -dimensional hyperbolic space such as continuity, and we also define a new hyperbolic width as the extension of Leichtweiss’ width function. Then we prove a characterization theorem of bodies of constant width regarding the aforementioned notions of hyperbolic width. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 1.

arxiv-2308-14709.title: An adaptive optics upgrade for the Automated Planet Finder Telescope using an adaptive secondary mirror
arxiv-2308-14709.creator: Rachel Bowens-Rubin, Arjo Bos, Philip Hinz, Bradford Holden, Matt Radovan
arxiv-2308-14709.description: Abstract As we enter the era of TESS and JWST, instrumentation that can carry out radial velocity measurements of exoplanet systems is in high demand. We will address this demand by upgrading the UC Lick Observatory’s 2.4-meter Automated Planet Finder (APF) telescope with an adaptive optics (AO) system.

arxiv-2405-17526.title: Heavy-Ion Collisions as Probes of Nuclear Structure
arxiv-2405-17526.creator: Nicolas Miró Fortier, Sangyong Jeon, Charles Gale
arxiv-2405-17526.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nicolas Miró Fortier, Sangyong Jeon, Charles Gale. In this work, we perform a model-to-data comparison for U+U and Au+Au collisions performed at RHIC at s NN \sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 193 GeV 193\text{\,}\mathrm{GeV} and 200 GeV 200\text{\,}\mathrm{GeV} , using a multistage framework.

arxiv-2406-06534.title: Compressed Meta-Optical Encoder for Image Classification
arxiv-2406-06534.creator: Anna Wirth-Singh, Jinlin Xiang, Minho Choi, Johannes E. Fröch, Luocheng Huang, Shane Colburn, Eli Shlizerman, Arka Majumdar
arxiv-2406-06534.description: Abstract Optical and hybrid convolutional neural networks (CNNs) recently have become of increasing interest to achieve low-latency, low-power image classification and computer vision tasks. However, implementing optical nonlinearity is challenging, and omitting the nonlinear layers in a standard CNN comes at a significant reduction in accuracy.

arxiv-2406-14317.title: Maximum principle preserving time implicit DGSEM for nonlinear scalar conservation laws
arxiv-2406-14317.creator: Florent Renac
arxiv-2406-14317.description: Abstract This work concerns the analysis of the discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM) with implicit time stepping for the numerical approximation of nonlinear scalar conservation laws in multiple space dimensions. We consider either the DGSEM with a backward Euler time stepping, or a space-time DGSEM discretization to remove the restriction on the time step.

arxiv-2407-06557.title: Comparison of Optimizers for Fault Isolation and Diagnostics of Control Rod Drives
arxiv-2407-06557.creator: Ark Ifeanyi, Jamie Coble
arxiv-2407-06557.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ark Ifeanyi, Jamie Coble. This paper explores the optimization of fault detection and diagnostics (FDD) in the Control Rod Drive System (CRDS) of GE-Hitachi’s BWRX-300 small modular reactor (SMR), focusing on the electrically powered fine motion control rod drive (FMCRD) servomotors. Leveraging the coordinated motion of multiple FMCRDs for control rod adjustments, the study proposes a deep learning approach, utilizing one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN)-based autoencoders for anomaly detection and encoder-decoder structured 1D CNN classifiers for fault classification.

arxiv-2410-07055.title: Transients by Black Hole Formation from Red Supergiants: Impact of Dense Circumstellar Matter
arxiv-2410-07055.creator: Daichi Tsuna, Xiaoshan Huang, Jim Fuller, Anthony L. Piro
arxiv-2410-07055.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Daichi Tsuna, Xiaoshan Huang, Jim Fuller, Anthony L. Piro. Failed supernovae (SNe), which are likely the main channel for forming stellar-mass black holes, are predicted to accompany mass ejections much weaker than typical core-collapse SNe. We conduct a grid of one-dimensional radiation hydrodynamical simulations to explore the emission of failed SNe from red supergiant progenitors, leveraging recent understanding of the weak explosion and the dense circumstellar matter (CSM) surrounding these stars.

arxiv-2502-03741.title: On the characterization of graphs with tree 3-spanners
arxiv-2502-03741.creator: Lan Lin, Yixun Lin
arxiv-2502-03741.description: Abstract Abstract. The tree spanner problem for a graph G is as follows: For a given integer k , is there a spanning tree T of G (called a tree k -spanner) such that the distance in T between every pair of vertices is at most k times their distance in G ?

arxiv-2503-07869.title: Carpe Diem: Critical Learning Period-Aware Contract-Based Incentives for Federated Learning Thanks: Thanh Linh Nguyen and Quoc-Viet Pham (Corresponding Author) are with the School of Computer Science and Statistics, Trinity College Dublin, The University of Dublin, Dublin 2, D02PN40, Ireland (e-mail
arxiv-2503-07869.creator: Thanh Linh Nguyen, Dinh Thai Hoang, Diep N. Nguyen, Quoc-Viet Pham
arxiv-2503-07869.description: Abstract Critical learning periods ( CLPs ) in federated learning (FL) refer to early stages during which low-quality contributions (e.g., sparse training data availability, strategic non-participation) can permanently impair the performance of the global model owned by the model owner (i.e., a cloud server).

arxiv-2512-01036.title: A Word Sampler for Well-Typed Functions
arxiv-2512-01036.creator: Breandan Considine
arxiv-2512-01036.description: Abstract . We describe an exact sampler for a simply-typed, first-order functional programming language. Given an acyclic finite automaton, α ∅ \alpha_{\varnothing} , it samples a random function uniformly without replacement from well-typed functions in ℒ ⁡ ( α ∅ ) \mathcal{L}(\alpha_{\varnothing}) .

arxiv-2512-23928.title: SRM at 30: Lessons from Early Data-Centric Networking and Their Impact on Named Data Networking
arxiv-2512-23928.creator: Tianyuan Yu, Adam Thieme, Junxiao Shi, Lan Wang, Lixia Zhang
arxiv-2512-23928.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tianyuan Yu, Adam Thieme, Junxiao Shi, Lan Wang, Lixia Zhang. A 1995 SIGCOMM paper, “A Reliable Multicast Framework for Light-weight Sessions and Application-Level Framing”, commonly known as SRM, explored a fundamentally new approach to reliable multiparty data delivery. Rather than adapting established sender-driven reliable unicast mechanisms to multicast, as most contemporaneous proposals did, SRM introduced a data-centric model in which data receivers recover losses by explicitly requesting missing data.

britannica-1911-stephen-sir-leslie.title: Stephen, Sir Leslie (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-stephen-sir-leslie.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-stephen-sir-leslie.description: Article 'Stephen, Sir Leslie' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. and literary critic, grandson of James Stephen (1758–1832), master in chancery, a friend of Wilberforce, and author of a book called Slavery Delineated, and son of Sir James Stephen (1789–1859), colonial under-secretary for many years, and author of Essays on Ecclesiastical Biography, was born at Kensington Gore on the 28th of November 1832.

plos-pone-0355739.creator: Nabila Masud, Catherine Fonder, Bridget McGovern, Md Hasibul Hasan Hasib, William J Jackson, Dulce C Resendiz, Carley Rivers, Sarah A Bentil
plos-pone-0355739.description: The effects of blast-induced traumatic brain injury on brain cellular mechanics and differentiation

pmc-10631381.title: Effectiveness of the spirometry-based motivational intervention to quit smoking: RESET randomised trial
pmc-10631381.creator: Francisco Martín-Luján, Antoni Santigosa-Ayala, Meritxell Pallejà-Millán, Cristina Rey-Reñones, Felipe Villalobos, Rosa Solà, the researchers of the RESET study
pmc-10631381.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundThe effectiveness of providing feedback on spirometry results for smoking cessation remains inconclusive according to the current evidence.ObjectivesTo assess the effectiveness of a motivational intervention based on spirometry results in achieving prolonged smoking abstinence (12 months post-intervention).Design and SettingA randomised, controlled, observer-blinded, multicentre clinical trial was conducted (from January 2012 to December 2015) in 20 primary healthcare centres in the Tarragona province, Spain.MethodsParticipants, active smokers aged 35–70 without known respiratory disease, were recruited from primary healthcare centres by family doctors and nurses.

pmc-11511329.title: Anthropometric Profile and Position-Specific Changes in Segmental Body Composition of Professional Football Players Throughout a Training Period
pmc-11511329.creator: Wiktoria Staśkiewicz-Bartecka, Karolina Krupa-Kotara, Mateusz Rozmiarek, Ewa Malchrowicz-Mośko, Mateusz Grajek, Saioa Agirre Elordui, Jokin Urriolabeitia Razkin, Arkaitz Castañeda Babarro, Andrew Hatchett
pmc-11511329.description: Body and anthropometric profiles of football players vary depending on the physiological and technical demands imposed by different positions. The aim of this study was to evaluate the body composition of professional soccer players in relation to their position on the field during a training macrocycle.

pmc-12593874.title: The role of NGOs in mainstreaming services for podoconiosis into healthcare facilities: the case of two NGOs in Ethiopia
pmc-12593874.creator: Kibur Engdawork, Getnet Tadele, Papreen Nahar, Gail Davey, Shahaduz Zaman
pmc-12593874.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundNon-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) have played an important role in supporting progress towards the goals of the WHO Neglected Tropical Disease (NTD) Roadmap 2021-30. Several NGOs have shifted from directly delivering NTD services to mainstreaming them to existing health systems. There is little information about the NGOs themselves – their organisational environments and their influence in mainstreaming NTD services and associated challenges.

pmc-12619327.title: Generation of hTERT-immortalized human mesenchymal stromal cells with optical and magnetic labels for in vivo transplantation and tracking
pmc-12619327.creator: Anna N. Gabashvili, Daria D. Namestnikova, Mikhail V. Gulyaev, Irina B. Pevzner, Alexey D. Bocharnikov, Natalya A. Alexandrushkina, Anastasiya V. Ryabova, Maria V. Efremova, Viktoria A. Sarkisova, Tatiana V. Tarasova, Stepan S. Vodopyanov, Pavel I. Makarevich, Petr I. Nikitin
pmc-12619327.description: BackgroundMesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) are the focus of increasing research as a potential therapeutic agent for a range of nervous system diseases, due to their unique capacity for self-renewal and differentiation. The subsequent tracking of cells post-transplantation into the organism is of pivotal significance, as it elucidates their fate, distribution, and enables the timely monitoring of any adverse effects.

pmc-12827283.title: Fourier-plane wavefront and SLM aberration characterization via iterative scanning of beam deflector segments
pmc-12827283.creator: Antoni J. Wojcik, Dilawer Singh, Ayan Rakshit, Hannah J. Joyce, Timothy D. Wilkinson
pmc-12827283.description: This study presents a method for characterizing the effective incident wavefront in the Fourier plane, eliminating the need to decouple measurement and application. The amplitude and phase of this wavefront are cumulatively affected by the incident beam, the curvature of the backplane, and the defocus introduced by the Fourier lens.

pmc-13271926.title: Peripheral cytotoxic immune profiles in hepatobiliary surgical patients
pmc-13271926.creator: Zhen Li, Dongping Yu, Lingyong Liu, Qi Zuo, Jiaqi Wang, Xiangjuan Jiao, Zhi Duan, Dong Chen
pmc-13271926.description: BackgroundPerforin and granzyme B are key effector molecules of cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) and natural killer (NK) cells. Their expression profiles in hepatobiliary surgical patients and the relative contributions of disease-specific versus host factors remain unclear.MethodsIn this retrospective cross-sectional study, 245 consecutive hepatobiliary surgical inpatients were enrolled.

pmc-13347403.title: From localization to distribution: revisiting the functional organization of the extrastriate body area
pmc-13347403.creator: Vojtěch Smekal, Lena L M Beckers, Marta Poyo Solanas, Beatrice de Gelder
pmc-13347403.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The extrastriate body area is a functional region of the human brain located in the lateral occipitotemporal cortex and was originally identified by its greater activation in response to images of human bodies compared with several other object categories. In subsequent research, the extrastriate body area was associated with a wide range of cognitive functions and processes localized to a substantial portion of the posterior cortex.

pmc-13380442.title: Isotype-switched antibodies originating from tertiary lymphoid structures can antagonize ovarian cancer progression
pmc-13380442.creator: Gunjan Mandal, Subir Biswas, Carmen M. Anadon, Baishali Tamuli, Ricardo A. Chaurio, Luis U. Lopez-Bailon, Noah Plappert, Dayan Carrion-Estrada, Jessica A. Mine, Chun-Hsiang Lai, Angela Per Moreno, Joseph Johnson, Carlos M. Moran-Segura, Bin Fang, Douglas Marchion, Neelkamal Chaudhary, Kathryn L. Ter
pmc-13380442.description: SummaryMany epithelial cancers orchestrate prognostically significant intratumoral tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs), yet the mechanisms behind their antitumor activity remain unclear. Here we show that intratumoral TLS in ∼14% of human high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) harbor highly oligoclonal B cells expressing IgA or IgG, which are not found in distant tumor regions.

pmc-13607237.title: Assessing Gamma Index Sensitivity to Selected Linear Accelerator Mechanical Errors Using Various Dosimetric Systems
pmc-13607237.creator: Hande Bas Ayata, Gokhan Aydin, Emrah Gokay Ozgur, Zeynep Ozen, Talip Celik, Ozcan Gundogdu
pmc-13607237.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) for stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) involves highly modulated dose distributions and steep dose gradients, increasing the importance of patient-specific quality assurance (QA). Gamma index analysis is widely used for comparing measured and treatment planning system (TPS)-calculated dose distributions; however, its sensitivity to small systematic mechanical errors remains controversial, particularly across different detector systems and normalization methods.
